Link record: commissioning loss 8.65 dB at 1550. A-TX launch spec -1 to +2 dBm. Currently TX power avg ~0.76 dBm (call_id 7). RX power historically ~ -11.2 dBm avg, now ~ -13.4 dBm avg. That's about 2.2 dB drop.

So fiber loss = TX - RX - attenuator? Actually RX measured at receiver input after attenuator. So link loss = TX - (RX + attenuator?) Let's think: TX -> fiber -> ODF -> attenuator -> RX. So RX = TX - fiber_loss - attenuator. So fiber_loss = TX - RX - attenuator. Historically: TX 0.76, RX -11.21, attenuator 3 dB => fiber_loss = 0.76 - (-11.21) -3 = 8.97 dB. Close to commissioning 8.65 dB, reasonable.

Now after degradation: TX 0.77, RX -13.39, attenuator 3 => fiber_loss = 0.77 - (-13.39) -3 = 11.16 dB. Increase ~2.2 dB.

OTDR from A: event 1 at 0.011 km distance, reflective loss 2.42 dB. That's at A-ODF. Normally connector loss should be ~0.1-0.3 dB. 2.42 dB is high. Reflectance -26.3 dB indicates reflection, maybe dirty or damaged. The event is at 0.011 km, essentially at launch point. Map to A-ODF.

OTDR from B: event 10 at 38.103 km fibre from B, loss 2.43 dB reflective, reflectance -26.7 dB. That's the A-ODF reflection seen from far end. Matches.

So fault appears at A-ODF connector.

OTDR shows reflective loss 2.42 dB, not typical for just dirty? Could be damaged connector or dirty. Connector end faces cannot be inspected remotely. For connector fault submit dirty_connector with clean_connector unless evidence shows damaged. Evidence shows loss 2.42 dB reflective, reflectance -26.3 dB. That's a high loss, but reflective. Could be dirty or damaged. The cleaning attempt didn't improve. Site note says cleaned with click cleaner after low Rx reported. No change in Rx power. So cleaning didn't help.
